chunks: Ahmad ibn Ziyad al-Hamdani (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from al-Sadiq, Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father al-Husayn (peace be upon them).

He said: The Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) was asked about the meaning of the saying of Allah's Messenger (peace be upon him and his family): 'Indeed, I am appointing as Successors among you, the Two Weighty Things, the Book of Allah and my Family.' Who is the Family? So he said: I, Hasan, Husayn, and the nine Imams from the offspring of Husayn, their ninth being their Guided One and their Rising One. They will not separate from the Book of Allah, nor will it separate from them, until they approach Allah's Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) at his basin.
ai.seo_question: Who are the 'Two Weighty Things' and the 'Family' in the Hadith al-Thaqalayn according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* explicitly defines the 'Ahl al-Bayt' in the Hadith al-Thaqalayn as the Prophet, Ali, Hasan, Husayn, and the nine Imams descending from Husayn, culminating in the Mahdi. It emphasizes their inseparable bond with the Quran, asserting that they will not be separated from it until they reunite with the Prophet at his Hawd (Pool) on the Day of Judgment. This establishes the Imams as the living, infallible interpreters of the Divine Text within Shia theology.
